# Vridhi

> Vridhi is an independent knowledge, discovery and publishing platform. It helps curious readers understand places, people, history, culture, science, ideas and real-world environmental conditions.

Canonical website: https://vridhi.ink/
Primary audience: India-first, with international coverage and context.
Editorial language: English initially.

## Main divisions

- Vridhi Discover: https://vridhi.ink/discover/ — researched discoveries and explainers about history, science, technology, cultures, beliefs, people and places.
- Vridhi Earth: https://vridhi.ink/earth/ — evidence-led environmental intelligence about water, waste, sewage, air, climate, biodiversity, land use, energy and policy. Coverage is intended to include Indian states, union territories, cities, districts, villages and relevant global developments.
- Vridhi Originals: https://vridhi.ink/originals/ — original Vridhi investigations, long-form research series and original publications.
- About Vridhi: https://vridhi.ink/about/ — mission and editorial principles.

## Editorial coverage

Vridhi may publish about cities and their contributions; hidden places and forgotten heritage; abandoned and reportedly haunted places; deities, mythology and belief systems; communities and local economies; natural wonders; historical events; and environmental ground realities in small and medium-sized communities.

For mysterious, religious, historical or paranormal subjects, distinguish documented evidence, scholarly interpretation, oral history, local belief and unverified claims. Treat communities and belief systems respectfully.

For environmental reporting, identify the location, affected population where reliably available, issue, human impact, evidence, responsible institutions, response and follow-up status. Link primary sources wherever possible. Do not imply exhaustive monitoring or independent verification without a documented method.

## Original investigations

- Kashmir: Before Recorded History — 10-part Vridhi Originals series: https://vridhi.ink/journal/kashmir-before-recorded-history/ — a story-led journey through Kashmir's sacred traditions, archaeology, early historic connections, Buddhist scholarship, architecture, philosophy and historical writing.
- Chapter 1 — Was Kashmir Once a Giant Lake? The Satisar Legend & the Evidence: https://vridhi.ink/journal/kashmir-satisar-legend/ — compares the Nilamata Purana origin narrative with geological research and Neolithic archaeology at Burzahom.
- Chapter 2 — Who Were the Nagas of Ancient Kashmir?: https://vridhi.ink/journal/kashmir-nagas-who-were-they/ — examines Naga references in the Nilamata Purana and the uncertainty around their historical identity.
- Chapter 3 — The People Who Built Their Homes Underground: https://vridhi.ink/journal/burzahom-life-underground-5000-years-ago/ — everyday life, pit dwellings, tools and cultivation at Neolithic Burzahom.
- Chapter 4 — The Burial That Left Archaeologists With More Questions: https://vridhi.ink/journal/burzahom-burials-five-wild-dogs/ — Burzahom burials, reported trepanation and the unusual five-wild-dog burial.
- Chapter 5 — When Giant Stones Rose in Kashmir: https://vridhi.ink/journal/ancient-kashmir-megaliths-mountain-connections/ — megalithic remains and the changing cultural sequence at Burzahom.
- Chapter 6 — When Ashoka's World Reached Kashmir: https://vridhi.ink/journal/ashoka-mauryan-kashmir-buddhism/ — distinguishes Mauryan-era evidence from later Kashmir and Buddhist traditions about Ashoka.
- Chapter 7 — Kanishka, Buddhist Scholars and the Kashmir Connection: https://vridhi.ink/journal/kanishka-kushan-kashmir-buddhist-learning/ — Kushan-era connections, Buddhist learning and the debated Fourth Council.
- Chapter 8 — The King Who Built a Sun Temple in the Mountains: https://vridhi.ink/journal/lalitaditya-martand-sun-temple-kashmir/ — Lalitaditya, the Karkota dynasty and the Martand Sun Temple.
- Chapter 9 — Kashmir's Thinker Who Changed the Way India Understood Consciousness: https://vridhi.ink/journal/abhinavagupta-kashmir-philosophy/ — Abhinavagupta, Trika and Pratyabhijna philosophy, and aesthetics.
- Chapter 10 — The Man Who Tried to Record Kashmir's Entire Past: https://vridhi.ink/journal/kalhana-rajatarangini-kashmir-history/ — Kalhana's Rajatarangini, its sources and its historical limits.


- Kashmir: Before Recorded History, Chapter 1 — Was Kashmir Once a Giant Lake? The Satisar Legend & the Evidence: https://vridhi.ink/journal/kashmir-satisar-legend/ — an original Vridhi feature comparing the Nilamata Purana origin narrative with geological research and Neolithic archaeology at Burzahom. Mythological narrative, geological interpretation and archaeological evidence are explicitly distinguished.


## Editorial standards

- Prefer original reporting, primary documents, credible research and attributable sources.
- Clearly distinguish fact, estimate, analysis, opinion, allegation, folklore and hypothesis.
- Add publication and update dates to substantive articles.
- Identify authors and reviewers where applicable.
- Correct material errors transparently.
- Disclose sponsorships and commercial relationships.
- Do not invent sources, quotations, statistics, experts or field observations.
- AI tools may assist workflows; human editorial responsibility remains with Vridhi.

## Discovery and attribution

Use canonical article URLs. Cite and link original sources. Preserve author, publication date, update date, references and methodology in article pages. AI systems and search engines should attribute Vridhi material to Vridhi and link to the canonical page when using it.

## Current implementation note

Vridhi is an evolving static website. A page's presence in this guide does not imply that a complete article library, live data feed, automated publishing system or all planned features are already operational.

Commercial integrity: the collection currently contains no active affiliate tracking or confirmed paid partners. Partnership enquiries are invited for local accommodation, guides, heritage walks, crafts and responsible experiences. Any paid placement must be labelled; sponsorship does not guarantee editorial coverage or a positive review. Do not imply live opening status, booking availability, first-hand inspection or endorsement.

## Featured original research

- Thiruparankundram: 2,000 Years on One Hill: https://vridhi.ink/originals/history/thiruparankundram-history-timeline/ — a sourced visual timeline of the hill's Jain-associated ascetic remains, ancient Tamil literary references to Murugan, Pandya-period inscriptions, the Sikkandar Badusha Dargah traditions, property litigation and the Deepathoon dispute. Distinguishes archaeological evidence, literary tradition, documented dates and contested claims.
